newsitem.title: USA: Texas electricity prices steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: Texas electricity prices steady to higher.

text.p: Wholesale electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) were steady to higher Tuesday as cool weather continued to dominate the state and natural gas prices held strong, sources said.
Temperatures were expected to reach highs in the 40s and 50s degrees Fahrenheit through most of Texas on Tuesday, but return to more normal, warmer levels from December 1 to 5.
Spot Texas natural gas prices climbed Tuesday by more then five cents to the low $3.70s per million British thermal units.
ERCOT firm, peak power for Wednesday delivery was assessed in the $30.00-33.00 range from talk at $31.50-32.50 on Monday, the brokers and marketers said.

Some utilities were said to be offering peak power at prices as high as $38.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), and some traders said next-day peak power exchanged hands at $34.00 per MWh, although the trades were not confirmed.
Off-peak non-firm ERCOT power transactions were pegged steady to lower at $16.00-18.00 from $17.00-18.00 on Monday.
ERCOT December peak power was said to be talked steady at $31.00-33.00, while January/February peak power was steady at $31.50-32.00, the sources said.
